summary: Traces how anti-fascist activists used clown costumes to mock neo-Nazi rallies from 2003 onward, and how in 2019 far-right internet users turned the Honkler and Clown World memes into nihilist, antisemitic dog whistles that spread to mainstream figures and street rallies.

evidence.note: Clown activism history starts with a UK clown army formed in 2003, active in Edinburgh
2005 Olympia, 2007 Knoxville and 2012 Charlotte neo-Nazi rallies met by clown counter-protesters
Swedish Nordic Resistance Movement rallies met by clowns, inspired by Finnish clowns vs Soldiers of Odin
Honkler appears on 4chan in early 2019, followed by a coordinated campaign to spread it
Extended segment on James Woods sharing a Honkler image traced from the Christchurch shooter
Clown World term found in 2017 far-right Discord chats tied to Unite the Right organisers
Host reads out slur-filled chan and Discord posts at length
Story ends with the September 2019 Boston Straight Pride Parade and clowns on both sides

notes: No theme for memes or internet subculture beyond tech-internet. Primary theme chosen as fascism-far-right since the meme spans the broader far right, with nazism secondary for the explicitly neo-Nazi groups and chan origins. Main span 2017-2019 covers the Clown World term through the Honkler spread; earlier clown protests are context for the reversal.
